evidence.quote: Question 44. — Let f ∈ Aut[C3] be any polynomial automorphism such that λ(f)2 > λ(f−1). Prove the existence of a projective compactification X of C3 such that the induced birational map f : X 99K X admits a super-attracting fixed point p on the divisor at infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f\in\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ be a polynomial automorphism. For any polynomial self-map $g$ of $\mathbb{C}^N$, let $\deg(g)$ denote the maximum of the degrees of its coordinate components, and define the first dynamical degree
$$\lambda(g)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\deg(g^n)^{1/n}.$$
A projective compactification of $\mathbb{C}^3$ is a normal projective variety $X$ together with an open embedding $\mathbb{C}^3\hookrightarrow X$ whose complement $D=X\setminus\mathbb{C}^3$ is a (Weil) divisor, called the divisor at infinity. The automorphism $f$ induces a birational self-map $f_X\colon X\dashrightarrow X$. A fixed point $p\in X$ of $f_X$ is called super-attracting if $p$ lies in the regular locus of $f_X$ and the differential $df_X(p)$ is the zero linear map.

Assume that $\lambda(f)^2>\lambda(f^{-1})$. Prove that there exists a projective compactification $X$ of $\mathbb{C}^3$ such that the induced birational map $f_X\colon X\dashrightarrow X$ admits a super-attracting fixed point on the divisor at infinity.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in a recent survey on open problems for Hénon-type maps and polynomial automorphisms. No published resolution was found in searches; the question concerning existence of a compactification of C^3 producing a super-attracting fixed point at infinity for automorphisms with λ(f)^2 > λ(f^{-1}) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: A list of open problems concerning Hénon maps and polynomial automorphisms, including questions about projective compactifications and super-attracting fixed points.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in the survey.
